name: Lenslet array (a moulded micro-lens face over a black matrix)
process: A light-field display's front: an array of small lenses, moulded or embossed in a clear layer on the pane's face, each over one group of the panel's pixels; between and behind the lenses a black matrix absorbs the light that falls on it. Each lens is an optically smooth surface, so a lamp seen in the array is repeated as one small glint in every lens: the face's reflection is spread over the lenses' range of slopes rather than blurred.

optics.text: Integral imaging places a lens array over an image plane at the lenses' focal distance, so each lens shows the viewer the pixel its direction selects.
optics.source: G. Lippmann, 'Epreuves reversibles donnant la sensation du relief', Journal de Physique Theorique et Appliquee 7 (1908) 821-825; F. Okano, H. Hoshino, J. Arai and I. Yuyama, 'Real-time pickup method for a three-dimensional image based on integral photography', Applied Optics 36(7) (1997) 1598-1603

unverified.field: the lenses' pitch, sag and the reflection's spread
unverified.reason: No maker's figures were read: the working's haze stands for the spread of the lenses' slopes, and its relief for their sag, as first values.
